headlines.article_text: Amazon, Intel shares fall after earnings amid AI spending concerns Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Intel shares fell 29% on Friday, posting the stock's worst day since the 1970s. The chipmaker issued weaker-than-expected guidance, citing ongoing softness in the PC market. Amazon also sold off following an earnings miss. In this article AMZN INTC Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan speaks during a keynote presentation at Computex in Taipei on June 2, 2026. Cheng Yu-chen | Afp | Getty Images Intel shares plummeted 29% on Friday, their worst day since the 1970s, after the chipmaker issued weaker-than-expected guidance due to a plant shutdown in Israel and ongoing softness in the PC market. It's a major setback for CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who was hired in March 2025, and has since been on a campaign to revive the company after it missed out on the early years of the artificial intelligence boom. Intel's plunge is also a big hit to the Trump administration, which led the U.S. government into taking a 10% stake in the company over a year ago. While it's still a profitable investment, the value of those holdings dropped by about $12 billion on Friday. Nvidia also took a big stake in Intel, and its stock dropped by about $6 billion in value. Heading into Thursday's earnings report, Intel shares were up about 150% this year, buoyed by demand for central processors, which are becoming critical to agentic AI workloads. Analysts at D.A. Davidson downgraded the stock to neutral from buy on Friday in a report titled, "Not fixed yet." "We understand the PC market is being impacted at the industry level," the analysts wrote. "However it is hard to justify the current multiple when weakness is so significant." Amazon and Intel stock chart Amazon shares also sold off on Friday, slipping 1.4%, after the company reported a third-quarter miss on the top and bottom line while maintaining its capital expenditure forecast for 2026 of $220 billion. Amazon also reported negative free cash flow for the second consecutive quarter, and a big increase from the previous period. The Nasdaq Composite slid 2.9%, capping off a week of rough tech earnings. Alphabet on Thursday suffered its worst day on record, plunging more than 12%. The stock fell again on Friday. Other semiconductor names also notched declines. Chip giant Nvidia fell 4%, while Broadcom dropped more than 5% and mobile chipmaker Qualcomm tumbled 11%. Not a 'moment of reckoning' Investors are growing nervous about the massive AI spending from the tech giants and whether their investments will pay off. "I don't think this is a moment of reckoning but I think it's a moment where investors should take a long thought about how positioning across the space still remains crowded even though the fundamentals are strong," Matt Orton, chief market strategist at Raymond James, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Friday. For Intel, the disappointing forecast reflects a PC market that's getting hammered due to soaring costs for memory and other components. Global PC shipments declined 4% in the second quarter from a year earlier, according to Counterpoint Research . Analysts were expecting revenue of $17.1 billion and EPS of 43 cents, according to LSEG. "We see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," Intel finance chief David Zinsner, said in the release. "We will continue making disciplined investments in capacity and working capital to increase supply and support future growth." The guidance also accounts for the effects of an explosion at a fab in Israel that killed two workers and seriously injured a third earlier this month. The incident will cost the company about $600 million in lost revenue over two quarters, Zinsner said. Tan said the explosion, which he called an "unfortunate and tragic accident," caused an "extended shutdown" at the plant, impacting shipments of 10-nanometer chips. Key to Tan's turnaround effort is Intel's foundry business, which has struggled to find its footing. Intel is the only U.S.-based manufacturer of advanced logic chips, and is now in high-volume production of its most advanced 18A chip out of its new fab in Arizona, providing an alternative to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co . Its next Arizona fab is expected to begin operations by the end of 2028. Intel still has no external customers for its new chips. "We're going to have a couple of customers ready to announce the next two quarters," Tan said on the call, adding that Intel is making "tremendous progress" on its coming 14A chips. headlines.article_text: Reddit plunges 29% after issuing weak outlook for its worst day ever Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Reddit fell 29.22% on Friday, wrapping its worst day since the company went public in 2024. The social media company reported weak sales guidance in its third-quarter earnings report. Reddit also announced it will test requiring users to log in to use the platform as AI continues to hit search referral numbers. In this article RDDT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:00 01:00 Reddit shares fall double digits on lighter-than-expected daily active users Closing Bell: Overtime Shares of Reddit cratered 29.22% on Friday, the worst drop since becoming a public company in 2024, after the company forecast weak fourth-quarter sales in its latest earnings report . The previous record low was set on July 31, when the stock dropped 20.99%. The social media company on Thursday projected fourth-quarter sales between $1 billion and $1.03 billion, below analysts' estimates of $1.05 billion. Reddit reported Q3 sales growth of 53% over a year ago, weaker than previous quarters, but beat Wall Street expectations on both earnings and revenue. The report comes as the company has seen a shift in its search referral traffic with the rise of Google's AI Overview. In an interview with CNBC, Reddit CEO Steve Huffman said search-referral traffic from Google went "down meaningfully in this quarter" due to AI. Reddit announced on Thursday that it plans to test requiring users to log in to access content, a dramatic change from a site whose community-based discussion content has become synonymous with the open internet. Google's shift towards pushing AI overviews in search results coincided with the change, intended to help boost the number of logged-in users that are more active on the platform, which in turn helps the company's advertising business, according to Huffman. "Reddit is the last platform to provide basically unfettered logged-out access, and that's largely because of me. I've been holding that line," Huffman said. "I think users will probably go through the same understanding that I have, which is that it's a sign of the times. It's an evolution of how these platforms work." Multiple analysts downgraded the stock following Reddit's disappointing results, with Citizens noting that "search changes highlight the problem with selling content to Google" and that as referral problems worsen, uncertainty around user growth amid the login requirement switch "puts more pressure on user monetization." — CNBC's Jonathan Vanian contributed to this report. headlines.article_text: Binance hack: Zhao asks Elon Musk to stop trolling Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Binance's cofounder Changpeng Zhao urged Elon Musk to stop mocking the exchange after it suffered a $6.3 billion hack. The SpaceX and Tesla CEO posted a series of emojis on X which appeared to poke fun at the attack, which has seen $3 billion in crypto assets frozen so far. In this article SPCX TSLA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Changpeng Zhao, co-founder of Binance Holdings Ltd., during the Bitcoin Asia conference in Hong Kong, China, on Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026. Chan Long Hei | Bloomberg | Getty Images Changpeng Zhao, the cofounder and former CEO of Binance , asked Elon Musk not to "troll" the company on Friday and instead "show some support" after the SpaceX CEO appeared to mock the embattled cryptocurrency exchange in a series of social media posts. After learning the world's largest crypto exchange had been hit by a $6.3 billion hack late Thursday, Musk posted several emojis, ranging from laughing to grimacing, on X. In response, Zhao reminded the SpaceX and Tesla CEO of Binance's equity stake in Musk's businesses. Binance’s SpaceX stake, which stems from an earlier investment in what was then-Twitter, is worth more than $1 billion, Zhao said. That's a tiny fraction of SpaceX's roughly $2 trillion valuation. "Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop," Zhao wrote. "Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion. Would appreciate if you show a little support. Thanks!" It's not the first time the pair has sparred online. In Nov. 2021, Binance suspended Dogecoin withdrawals because of a wallet glitch, a measure Musk called "shady". In reply, Zhao highlighted a major Tesla recall of almost 12,000 U.S. vehicles due to software glitches and hardware issues. Binance froze all withdrawals and deposits after the hack, which investigators suspect to be the work of North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit TraderTraitor. It has since restored deposits. Around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets have been frozen so far. Correction: Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao asked Elon Musk to "show some support." headlines.summary: Social media companies face thousands of lawsuits alleging they knowingly sought to addict children to their platforms, contributing ⁠to a youth mental health crisis.
headlines.article_text: Meta settles with teen during trial testing claims social media caused depression, eating disorders Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article META SNAP GOOGL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Facebook and Instagram icons are seen displayed on an iPhone. Jakub Porzycki | Nurphoto | Getty Images Meta Platforms has settled with a teen plaintiff who accused the company of designing Instagram and Facebook to be addictive, causing her mental health problems and disordered eating, attorneys for the plaintiff said ⁠on Friday. The settlement came after jury selection began on Wednesday for a trial that was slated to test the claims of ​two teens, identified as S.J. and ​K.D.B., against Meta and Snapchat ​parent Snap Inc . Meta had settled with S.J. days before the trial, so Friday's settlement with K.D.B. means the trial is expected to proceed against Snap only. "We remain committed to improving safety for kids on social media apps ⁠and ‌holding tech companies accountable, and we are pleased to have brought ⁠this matter to a just resolution on behalf of our client," Emily Jeffcott, an attorney for K.D.B., said in a statement. The trial is the second in Los Angeles state court over claims brought by young people who say they became addicted to social media ‌after Meta, Snap, TikTok and Alphabet's YouTube designed their platforms to encourage compulsive use. S.J. and K.D.B. had previously settled with TikTok and YouTube. The case was selected among the thousands of ​pending lawsuits as a test case, so the jury's verdict could influence how the companies and plaintiffs resolve similar cases. S.J., a 16-year-old girl from Illinois, and K.D.B., an 18-year-old from Mississippi, say they began using YouTube as early as age 3 and the other platforms around age ⁠9, developing compulsive habits they blame on features such as autoplay and infinite scroll. The companies have rejected claims their platforms were designed ‌to addict young people, and say they have taken action to make ‌the apps safe places for young people to express themselves. Social media companies face thousands of lawsuits in federal and state courts by individuals, school districts, municipalities and other government entities alleging the companies knowingly sought to addict children to their platforms, contributing ⁠to a youth mental health crisis involving anxiety, depression and suicide. In the first case to go ⁠to trial, which ended in March, a Los Angeles jury found Meta and YouTube ⁠had been negligent and awarded a young woman $6 million in damages. The next two teens whose cases were selected for trials either settled or dropped their claims against the ​companies. The first school district chosen for trial settled with ‌all of the companies. In August, Meta struck settlements worth up to $18 billion with nearly every state and US territory to resolve lawsuits brought by attorneys general over the platforms' harm to teens and agreed to make changes to how Instagram and Facebook work for teens. Earlier this month, a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay a $25 billion penalty after ​a jury found the company misled Facebook users ‌about the privacy of their data and how it handles hate speech. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: INTC, LITE, SNDK, TWLO, COIN Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Here are some of the companies making headlines in midday trading. Semiconductor stocks — Chipmakers suffered Friday as technology stocks sold off and concern reemerged about the strength of the artificial intelligence trade. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) slumped 7%, Astera Labs ' stock tumbled 12%, shares of Qualcomm dropped 11% and Nvidia 's stock lost 4%. AI infrastructure plays — The iShares A.I. Innovation and Tech Active ETF (BAI) slumped more than 7%, and shares of Micron Technology slid more than 5%, Lumentum Holding s by more than 10% and Arista Networks by almost 8%, as stocks tied to the artificial intelligence buildout continued to lose air. CNBC's David Faber also said Friday that the proposed deal for Lumentum by Marvell Technology won't come at a big premium. Regeneron Pharmaceuticals — The biotech company's stock jumped 11%. Third-quarter results beat estimates, with Regeneron earning $20.07, excluding items, on revenue of $5.12 billion. The FactSet consensus sought $16.42 per share and $4.56 billion. For the full-year period, Regeneron is calling for non-GAAP gross margin on net product sales of about 86%, up from its earlier guidance of 84% to 85%. Sandisk — Shares fell 12% even after the data storage device manufacturer reported an earnings and revenue beat in its fiscal first-quarter financial report. It delivered adjusted earnings of $49.51 per share compared with analysts' estimates for $46.22, per LSEG. Sandisk also announced an eight-for-one forward stock split. Twilio — Shares dropped about 17% after the consumer engagement platform's current-quarter guidance reflected slowing organic revenue growth. Twilio sees fourth-quarter revenue in a range of $1.595 billion to $1.605 billion and year-over-year organic revenue growth in a range of 11% to 12%. In the third quarter, however, organic revenue grew 16% year over year. Roblox — Shares of the gaming platform shed 20% after the company gave disappointing guidance for the fourth quarter. Projected bookings for the period range from $1.89 billion to $2 billion, while analysts anticipated $2 billion. Mondelez International — The company behind Sour Patch Kids and Oreo cookies saw its stock add more than 3%. Mondelez reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of 78 cents a share, topping the FactSet consensus estimate of 71 cents per share. FedEx Freight — Shares jumped 15% after the freight transportation services business gave strong guidance for the fourth quarter. FedEx Freight expects quarterly revenue between $2.3 billion and $2.37 billion, compared to $2.07 billion a year ago. It anticipates adjusted operating income between $185 million and $205 million, up from $162 million a year prior. Intel — Shares tumbled 29% after the chipmaker issued weaker-than-expected guidance for the fourth quarter . The company sees adjusted earnings per share of 25 cents on revenue ranging between $15 billion and $16 billion. That's below LSEG estimates of 43 cents in earnings per share and revenue of $17.1 billion. Rivian Automotive — Shares jumped over 8% after the electric vehicle maker reported better-than-expected third-quarter results. Rivian lost an adjusted 48 cents per share on revenue of $2.16 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG expected a loss of 62 cents per share on revenue of $1.99 billion. The company also increased its guidance on deliveries . Amazon — Shares slipped 1% after the e-commerce giant reported third-quarter results that missed analyst expectations. The company also posted negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion for the trailing 12-month period. Reddit — The company announced it will require users to log in to access its social media platform and issued weaker-than-expected revenue guidance for the fourth quarter. Shares tumbled 29%. Crypto-related stocks — Shares of Coinbase and Robinhood shed 12% and 8%, respectively, following one of the largest crypto hacks ever on Thursday when Binance reported an estimated $6.3 billion was affected. The company also estimates roughly $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets were frozen. Chevron — Shares added 1% after Chevron reported its net income surged nearly 200% to $9.9 billion in the third quarter. The company also posted better-than-expected revenue for the period. Exxon Mobil — Shares gained more than 1% after the oil giant's profits doubled to $15.4 billion from $7.5 billion in the year-earlier period. AstraZeneca — Shares of the biopharmaceutical company jumped over 7% following better-than-expected third-quarter earnings. The company reported core earnings of $2.79 per share on revenue of $16.21 billion. Analysts expected a profit of $2.60 per share on revenue of $16.05 billion. — CNBC's Michelle Fox, Scott Schnipper, Nick Wells and Darla Mercado contributed reporting.
